title: Sidorenko's Conjecture (Conjecture 1.2)
statement_text: For every bipartite undirected graph $H$ and every undirected graph $G$, $t_H(G) \geq t_{K_2}(G)^{e(H)}$.
context_text: Independently posed by Erdős–Simonovits and Sidorenko, this conjecture asserts that the Erdős–Rényi random graph minimises the homomorphism density of any bipartite graph. The paper systematically develops tournament analogues of this conjecture, defining tournament Sidorenko and tournament anti-Sidorenko properties and studying their structural characterisations.
paper_contribution: Develops tournament analogues of Sidorenko's conjecture: proves asymptotically tight bounds on the maximum number of edges in a tournament anti-Sidorenko digraph, gives novel constructions of tournament Sidorenko digraphs, and fully characterises which orientations of stars are tournament Sidorenko or tournament anti-Sidorenko.
paper_title: Variations on Sidorenko's conjecture in tournaments

title: Conjecture 1.12
statement_text: For every undirected tree, there exists some orientation that has the tournament anti-Sidorenko property.
context_text: For digraphs $D$ and $T$, the homomorphism density $t_D(T)=h_D(T)/v(T)^{v(D)}$ is the fraction of all maps $V(D)\to V(T)$ that are homomorphisms (send arcs to arcs). A digraph $D$ with $e(D)$ arcs is tournament anti-Sidorenko if $t_D(T)\le 2^{-e(D)}$ for every tournament $T$ (equivalently, every $n$-vertex tournament has at most $2^{-e(D)}n^{v(D)}$ labeled copies of $D$), i.e. $D$ is never more frequent than in a uniformly random tournament; it is tournament Sidorenko if $t_D(T)\ge(1-o(1))2^{-e(D)}$ for all tournaments $T$ (the $o(1)$ is due to tournaments having no loops). Examples of anti-Sidorenko digraphs are directed paths and directed cycles of length not divisible by 4. The authors show that a $k$-vertex tournament anti-Sidorenko digraph has at most $(1+o(1))k\log_2k$ arcs, which is tight. For trees, any orientation having a homomorphism to a single arc is tournament Sidorenko; they characterize orientations of stars $K_{1,s}$: such an orientation is tournament anti-Sidorenko if and only if the centre's in-degree and out-degree differ by at most one. The conjecture asks whether every undirected tree has an anti-Sidorenko orientation; the authors prove it for all trees with at most one vertex of even degree.
paper_title: Variations on Sidorenko's conjecture in tournaments
